WHAT WAS WRONG, in one line: the sum of the five's perdef ALONE scored +0.763, and the shipped formula scored +0.587. Every term stacked on top of perdef was subtracting signal. THREE were doing it. (1) The anchor was UNCAPPED in defenseVs' didx — teamDefense has always written min(99, anchor), this line did not, and anchorRaw = rimprot1 + 0.35 x rimprot2^2/99 runs past 99 on 902 of the 1,255 fives (max 131.3, Bucks '21). (2) `cover` refunded the perdef deficit of the four non-anchor defenders whenever the five had a big, so a bad perimeter five WITH a big read as a good perimeter five; its supposed paint-hunting gate, min(1, paintOrient x 2), is 1.00 against the reference five and against every real offense. (3) The discipline penalty was the LARGEST variance channel of drtgRef (sd 0.588 on a 5.84-point all-time range, i.e. up to ~73 dial points) and it pointed the wrong way: mean discipline of a five correlates +0.075 with WORSE real defence. Fouling is how good defences play.

THE PACKAGE, MEASURED STEP BY STEP before it was applied (mean within-season rho): shipped +0.587 · cap the anchor alone +0.568 · cover x0 alone +0.654 · discipline off alone +0.668 · cap + cover + discipline +0.742 · plus anchor 0.26 -> 0.13 onto perdef 0.42 -> 0.55 +0.758 · plus steals 0.20 -> 0.12 +0.762. Capping the anchor ALONE makes things slightly worse — which is why it is a package and not three rounds: the cap only pays once the refund it was propping up is gone.
